question: What is the length of IPv4 address in terms of nibble?
solution:
The correct answer is __**8 nibbles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The length of IPv4 address** in terms of nibble is** 8 nibbles.**
 
• The most used **IP version was IPv4**. In 1983, it was delivered to the ARPANET for creation.
 
• It is a frequently used IP modification.
 
• The **32-bit address** format is used by IPv4.
 
• There is a **dot (.) **between each binary bit in IPv4 and broadcast is supported. A dot represents a binary bit in IPv4 (.).
 
• IPv4 security allows encryption to maintain security and privacy.
 
• Redefining IPV4 addresses allows for faultless encoding. Because addressing is collectively done more successfully, routing is far more scalable and cost-effective.
 
• IP addresses come in two different sizes:** IPv4 (four bytes) and IPv6 (Sixteen bytes).**
 
• The RARP protocol allows a device with an IP address to retrieve information.
 
• The network layer is where IP Address operates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the world of computers and digital technology, a nibble is** four binary digits **or one-half of an eight-bit byte.
 
• One hexadecimal digit can conveniently represent a nibble.
